title: a-judge-declares-its-attendance
intention: EACH JUDGE REPORTS THAT IT RAN, NOT ONLY THAT IT OBJECTED. Today judge_constrain/survey/decompose/triage/hypothesize/validate each return a list of FINDING FRAGMENTS tagged {judge, finding, evidence, why_it_matters}. A judge that saw the packet and was satisfied returns nothing, and a judge that was never reached returns nothing, and the two are the same bytes. So the stage entry `installed_judges_find_nothing` can put in its ACTUAL which judges FIRED — it cannot put which judges PASSED. Close it by having the judge half of the record carry ATTENDANCE: every judge that ran appears, with its findings (possibly none) beside it, so the entry's EXPECTED can be the declared roster for that stage and its ACTUAL can be who showed up. A judge that stops running then makes the record SHORTER, which is the whole point of the record over the complaint list.
why: THE MYSTERY THE RULING WAS RAISED AGAINST IS STILL LIVE IN HALF OF EACH RECORD. Akien's lived symptom: "passing such a thing without inspecting it means passing a mystery if something downstream fails", and "we can backtrack and see exactly where something went awry even if it's not something we're specifically looking for yet." The eight stages' SHAPE checks now answer that — every check that ran is in the record with its expected beside its actual. The JUDGE checks do not: a judge silently deleted, renamed, or short-circuited by an early return reads on the record exactly like a judge that inspected the packet and approved it. Backtracking through a chart chain a month from now, the reader cannot tell which. That is the same failure the complaint list had, surviving inside the thing that replaced it — which is why it is filed rather than left in prose (Law 4: an IOU without a real ticket is itself the defect).
traces_to: Law 3 — nothing is known until measured. "The judges found nothing" is today an inference from silence, not a measurement; attendance makes it one.
Law 7 — errors are loud at diagnostic surfaces. A chart packet's proof record IS a diagnostic surface, and a judge that vanished is currently silent there.
Law 9 — red is the default. An unrun judge should read red, and today it reads exactly like green.
Ruling 2026-08-13 every-machine-carries-its-own-inspector-and-gate — this is that ruling's own residue, named by its own falsifier clause.

falsifier.proves_green: the six stage doors and the promotion-side sieves in cairn/machines/build_inspector are ONE implementation per stage (the `_judge_charted` wrapper composes the same pure judge the door does); the fix must keep that singleness — a roster the door knows and the sieve does not is the drift, not the fix.
falsifier.proves_red: RED on any of: (1) a declared roster that is derived by PARSING judge source for string literals rather than declared — that is a proxy, and a proxy for attendance is the thing being replaced; (2) a per-stage roster living anywhere but beside its judges (Law 6 — one owner); (3) the door and the promotion sieve disagreeing about who is on the roster; (4) attendance recorded for a judge that did not actually examine the packet — attendance must be emitted by the judge, not asserted by its caller.
falsifier.horizon: Re-read when the chart chain runs in anger against a real ticket and someone needs to backtrack a refusal. Until then this is a known-and-named gap, sized at six stages and roughly a dozen judges.

how.mechanism: Each judge returns an ATTENDANCE RECORD instead of only a findings list. Today a judge returns [] (nothing wrong) or [{judge, finding, evidence, why_it_matters}, ...]. After: a judge returns {judge: <name>, ran: true, findings: [...]} — always present when it ran, findings possibly empty. A judge that did not run is ABSENT from the list, not present with ran:false.
how.roster: Each stage declares its ELIGIBLE JUDGES beside its judge code — the roster. The roster is the entry's EXPECTED. The collected attendance records are the entry's ACTUAL. A judge missing from ACTUAL that is in EXPECTED is a red (judge didn't run). The roster lives in _judge_charted's stage configuration, not parsed from source.
how.single_implementation: The _judge_charted wrapper in inspector.py is the ONE place each judge is called. It already wraps every judge for both the door and the promotion sieve. Adding the attendance record here — wrapping the pure judge's return into {judge, ran, findings} — means the door and the sieve both get it without duplication.
how.entry_shape_change: The stage entry installed_judges_find_nothing changes from expected=[], actual=sorted-judges-that-objected TO expected=stage_roster, actual=sorted-judges-that-ran. The entry name itself changes to reflect the new semantics — it no longer measures silence.
how.eligibility: A judge may declare itself ineligible for a packet (an optional field is absent, a ref is missing). Ineligible judges are excluded from EXPECTED for that run, so their absence is legitimate rather than red. Eligibility is a predicate the judge declares, not a caller-side filter.
